newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: LINK network details future aims, sees expansion.
newsitem.headline: LINK network details future aims, sees expansion.

text.p: LINK (Logistics International Network) which groups family-owned freight forwarding companies said it plans to create new joint airfreight products and an interactive site on the Internet.

Jacques van den Berg, general manager of one of the eleven founding firms, Vitesse Air -- based near Amsterdam -- told Reuters by telephone from Sydney that the group's first assembly held in the Australian city had been successful.
"It is clear that we are going to grow, and there is now an interest in joining LINK from similar companies all over the world," he said in a telephone interview.

The group also includes Lynden International of the U.S., Master Freight International of Brazil, Northern Air Freight of Hong Kong, World International Cargo of Taiwan, Merstar International (Singapore) Pte Ltd, McTrans International Inc of South Korea, Lynair International (Australia), Inter-Speed of South Africa, Enterprise Airfreight of UK, Germany's Quick Cargo Service and CNT Air Express Inc of the Philippines.
Van den Berg said talks at the meeting focused on the creation of joint products, and said more details would be released next year.
In addition, the group will invest in the development of an interactive Internet site, to enable customers to make full use of the joint services of member companies.
He said 1997 will see more companies joining the group and LINK aims to facilitate membership by making its introductory process more flexible.
"We will aim for a total of 25 new members in the next year or so," he added.
LINK's next assembly is planned for September 1997, in Johannesburg. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
